record_title: Sharp coherence frontier for residual spikes in maximal-distance Kaczmarz
scientific_context: For maximal-distance Kaczmarz on m row-normalized equations with row coherence mu, the exact universal one-step normalized-residual amplification factor is piecewise: sqrt((m-1)(1+mu)^2/m) for mu <= 1/(m-1), and sqrt(1+(m-1)mu^2) thereafter. Universal stepwise residual monotonicity holds exactly through mu = sqrt(m/(m-1)) - 1. Explicit square nonsingular systems show sharpness, and a matching theta-approximate-selection frontier is derived.
limitations: Exact arithmetic and one-step analysis. The controlled quantity is the scale-invariant normalized residual ||D^{-1}(Ax-b)||_2, equal to the ordinary Euclidean residual only for unit-row systems. Pairwise coherence can be pessimistic for a fixed matrix. No iteration-complexity, finite-precision, asynchronous, block, or noisy/inconsistent-convergence claim is made. The Gauss-Southwell interpretation requires full row rank. Older relaxation and coordinate-relaxation literature leaves residual historical-equivalence risk.

artifact_inventory.description: Deterministic NumPy checks of the sharp matrix family, the coherence threshold, the approximate-selection extension, and random unit-row systems.
Verified numerical output with software versions, fixed seed, equality errors, threshold checks, and the largest observed normalized residual ratio relative to the bound.
